clue.text: Shoot an annoying person in capital

blocks.note: a bud is a young shoot on a plant
the indefinite article
a pest is a nuisance of a person

explanation.surface: A gunman takes aim at some irritating individual in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Budapest is the capital city of Hungary, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Simple when covered by writer

indicators.note: being covered by something means being enclosed within it

blocks.note: a Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Something is easy once an author has dealt with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic means elementary or plain, a synonym for simple.

clue.text: Diane taken over southern resort in a state of neglect

blocks.note: Di is short for Diane
abbreviation for south or southern
to repair to a place is to resort or go there

explanation.surface: Diane is driven past a run-down holiday town in the south.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday town but is the verb, as in 'resort to'. In a down clue, 'taken over' puts DI on top.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrepair is the condition of being neglected and in poor repair.

clue.text: Groom, stiffly formal before start of proceedings

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: prim means stiffly proper
the opening letter of proceedings

explanation.surface: A bridegroom stands rigidly correct before a ceremony begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Groom is the verb, not the bridegroom of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to make small adjustments to one's appearance, to groom oneself.

clue.text: Crawler to remain in class?

blocks.note: to stick is to stay put
taken as written
a sect is a group or class

explanation.surface: A sycophant wants to stay on in a school class.
explanation.walkthrough: Crawler suggests a toady, but here it is a creeping creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The stick insect is a slow-moving insect that creeps along twigs, so a crawler.

clue.text: Emphasise the importance of drama at university

blocks.note: a play is a piece of drama
a student in residence at university is said to be up

explanation.surface: Someone stresses how much theatre matters on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Being UP means in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To play up a point is an idiom for highlighting or stressing its significance.

clue.text: Girl touring one, an American state

indicators.note: touring means going all round, so the name encircles what follows

blocks.note: a girl's name
Roman numeral one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young woman travels around one of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a state in the southern US, on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: A short time to rest up in Black Sea resort

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
to lay something is to set it down at rest

explanation.surface: Someone takes a brief break at a seaside resort on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta is a resort town on the Crimean coast of the Black Sea, famous for the 1945 conference.

clue.text: Staff in Nelson upset after salesman's given a rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Workers are troubled at Nelson's after a sales agent gets a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: Given a rise suggests a pay increase, but in a down clue it turns the salesman upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Around Miami's centre, miss his subtle Japanese dishes

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter alone
something subtle is crafty and devious, so the letters before it are cunningly rearranged
the rearranged letters go around the single letter taken from the city's name

blocks.note: the central letter of the five-letter Miami
seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner in Florida passes up some delicate Japanese food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sashimi is the Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish, here pluralised as several servings.

clue.text: Nevertheless left, accompanied by the Queen's servant

blocks.note: but and nevertheless both introduce a contrast
standard abbreviation for left
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A royal servant departs anyway, alongside the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A butler is the chief manservant of a household, so a servant.

clue.text: Vulgar girl on board points to miserly types

indicators.note: something on board is inside a vessel, so the name sits within the pair of compass letters

blocks.note: cheap can mean tawdry or vulgar
two compass points, south and south
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A coarse woman on a ship points the way to some penny-pinchers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is an informal name for a stingy person who avoids spending.

clue.text: A matching jacket and pants with pocket fit the bill

blocks.note: to trouser money is to pocket it
to suit is to be just right

explanation.surface: A coordinated outfit with pockets is just what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is the American word for trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouser suit is a woman's outfit of jacket and trousers in the same fabric.

clue.text: A party causing bother

blocks.note: taken as written
a do is an informal party

explanation.surface: A rowdy celebration creates trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ado means fuss or trouble, as in much ado about nothing, a synonym for bother.

clue.text: Player's excellent hand?

blocks.note: surface reading: a card player has been dealt a very strong set of cards
setter's reading: an actor gets an enthusiastic round of applause, a 'hand', with the audience on its feet

explanation.walkthrough: Player suggests cards, but here it is an actor; a 'hand' is a burst of clapping, as in 'give them a big hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: When an audience rises to its feet to applaud a performer, that ovation is the highest form of the clapping called a hand.

clue.text: Fruit from Kansas dished out as well inside

indicators.note: dished out means served around, so the state's letters are distributed afresh
the phrase for also goes within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: six letters to be rearranged
too means also

explanation.surface: Produce from Kansas is served up too.
explanation.walkthrough: Saskatoon is also a Canadian city, but here it is the berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The saskatoon is a North American shrub whose purple berries are eaten as fruit.

clue.text: Unsafe to treat us injecting needle

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, so the irritation goes within the treating phrase

blocks.note: to do someone is to treat or serve them
taken as written
needle as irritation or annoyance

explanation.surface: A medical warning that being given an injection by needle is risky.
explanation.walkthrough: Needle looks like a syringe, but it means irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous means likely to cause harm, a synonym for unsafe.

clue.text: Check defaced copy

indicators.note: defaced read literally means losing its face, so the word loses its front letter

blocks.note: a check is a restraint or limitation

explanation.surface: Inspect a forgery that has been spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: Defaced suggests vandalism; here it means the first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitation is a replica or reproduction, a synonym for copy.

clue.text: Dog chewed up grannie's slipper

indicators.note: something chewed up is mangled out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fifteen letters to be rearranged, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A pet has gnawed an elderly woman's indoor shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: The springer spaniel is a breed of gundog, so an example of a dog.

clue.text: Include a theologian

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theology degree

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring a religious scholar into the group.
explanation.definitionFit: To add something is to put it in alongside the rest, a synonym for include.

clue.text: Leader in demonology needs to study fear

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of demonology
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: An expert in demons must research what terrifies people.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is great fear or apprehension, a synonym for fear.

clue.text: Kill terrible martinet in English river

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked or messed up, so the letters of the strict disciplinarian are rearranged
the rearranged letters are placed inside the name of the waterway

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to do away with a dreadful disciplinarian found in an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: To exterminate is to destroy completely, a stronger synonym for kill.

clue.text: Ancient Greek colony shown in edition I acquired

indicators.note: shown in says the answer is on display inside the words that follow

blocks.note: spans the end of edition, the I, and the start of acquired

explanation.surface: A settlement of the ancient Greeks appears in a book edition someone obtained.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the region of Greek settlements on the west coast of Asia Minor.

clue.text: Editor cutting staff? The opposite is correct

indicators.note: cutting means going into, so one part is placed inside another
the opposite tells the solver to swap which part goes inside which

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for editor
the staff of a firm are its men

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor slashes the workforce, and the reverse is right.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the editor would go inside the staff; the clue says reverse that, so the staff sits inside the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors, a synonym for correct as a verb.

clue.text: Cat in patch of ground by old church

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for old
Church of England
a lot is a plot of land

explanation.surface: A cat sits in a piece of land beside an ancient church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' puts the patch of ground after the old church, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild feline of the Americas, an example of a cat.

clue.text: Try fish the American way

blocks.note: a try or go, as in 'have a turn'
a freshwater predatory fish

explanation.surface: An invitation to go fishing in the style of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The American way' looks like it modifies the fishing, but it is the definition: a way, or road, in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnpike is a US toll highway, so literally a road or way in America.

clue.text: Scrabbling in dust, one leading a bare existence

indicators.note: scrabbling is frantic scratching about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone grubbing about in the dirt lives a simple, poor life.
explanation.walkthrough: A bare existence normally means poverty; here it means life without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes unclothed, so their life is literally bare.

clue.text: Awkward riddle put to Edward

blocks.note: to riddle is to sieve, that is, to strain
short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A tricky puzzle is posed to a man named Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddle looks like a puzzle, but here it is the coarse sieve used for soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A strained conversation is forced and uncomfortable, so awkward.
